user.title: Crop Steering setup

data_description.name: A name for the grow room, for example "Veg" or "Flower B". The integration uses the name in the entity IDs of the room, for example `number.crop_steering_veg_lights_on_hour`. The entity IDs of the room come from this name. The controller finds each setting by its exact entity ID. Use a short name that the operators can find on the dashboard. Do not use the name "Default".
data_description.drainage: How the runoff leaves the pots or the slabs in this room. Select "Flood tables or trays", "Free drain" or "Not sure". Flood tables or trays, or Not sure: the controller watches the room for a table that does not drain (CS-310). Free drain: the controller does not watch the room for CS-310. Select "Free drain" only when the runoff cannot collect under the pots or the slabs. CAUTION: Do not select "Free drain" for a room on flood tables. The controller then does not detect a table that does not drain, and the roots can stay in water.

manual_zones.title: Number of zones
manual_zones.description:
{info}

Count the zone valves in the room. Enter that number in the field.

data_description.num_zones: The number of zones in the room. Each zone has its own zone valve. You map the valve and the probes of each zone in the next step. The next step shows one set of fields for each zone. Enter one zone for each zone valve that the controller opens.

zones.title: Map the zones
zones.description:
{info}

Select each entity from its list. Make sure that each zone valve is the valve of that zone. After setup, do a test shot on each zone.

data_description.zone_1_switch: The switch entity that opens the zone valve of this zone. The controller sets this switch to on to start a shot and to off to end the shot. After each shot, it reads the switch back to confirm that the valve is closed. Select the switch that opens the valve of this zone, and no other switch. After setup, do a test shot on the zone. WARNING: Set the kill switch to off before you work on the valve or its wiring. While the kill switch is on, the controller can open the valve at any time. CAUTION: Do not map the valve of a different zone. The controller then gives water to the wrong zone, and that zone can flood or dry out.
data_description.zone_1_vwc: One or more substrate probes that give the moisture (VWC) of this zone, in %. Select a probe in a block that is typical of the zone. The controller uses the zone reading from these probes for its phase and shot decisions. With more than one probe, the zone reading is the average of the valid readings. The average does not reject an outlier. CAUTION: Do not map a probe from a different zone. The controller then waters this zone on the moisture of the other zone.
data_description.zone_1_ec: One or more substrate probes that give the pore EC of this zone. With more than one probe, the zone reading is the average of the probes. The controller uses the zone EC for its EC decisions. When pore EC reaches the maximum safe EC, the controller can give a flush shot. Select probes that report pore EC. CAUTION: Do not map an EC probe from a different zone. The controller then flushes or doses this zone on the EC of the other zone.
data_description.zone_1_plant_count: The number of plants in this zone. A new room starts at a generic value, not a value for your room. The controller multiplies the substrate volume per plant and the dripper flow by this number. Increase: each shot of the zone gives more water. Decrease: each shot gives less water. CAUTION: Do not keep the generic value. A wrong plant count gives wrong shot volumes and wrong daily water limits.

WARNING: Set the kill switch to off before you work on the valve or its wiring. While the kill switch is on, the controller can open the valve at any time. CAUTION: Do not map the valve of a different zone. The controller then gives water to the wrong zone, and that zone can flood or dry out.
data_description.zone_16_vwc: One or more substrate probes that give the moisture (VWC) of this zone, in %. Select a probe in a block that is typical of the zone. The controller uses the zone reading from these probes for its phase and shot decisions. With more than one probe, the zone reading is the average of the valid readings. The average does not reject an outlier. CAUTION: Do not map a probe from a different zone. The controller then waters this zone on the moisture of the other zone.
data_description.zone_16_ec: One or more substrate probes that give the pore EC of this zone. With more than one probe, the zone reading is the average of the probes. CAUTION: Do not map an EC probe from a different zone. The controller then flushes or doses this zone on the EC of the other zone.

data_description.plumbing: The equipment between the water and the zone valves: zone valves only, a pump, a main-line valve, or both. The pump and main-line switches below must agree with this selection. Setup refuses to save when the switches do not agree. The controller refuses to water a room where they no longer agree. It never opens a zone valve with no pump in a room that needs its pump. If water comes out only while a pump runs, select a type with a pump. CAUTION: Do not select a type without a pump for a room that needs its pump. The zone valve then opens with no pump, and the plants get no water.
data_description.pump_switch: The switch that runs the water pump. Map it when the plumbing above has a pump. Leave it EMPTY when it does not. The controller starts the pump before it opens the main-line valve and the zone valve. It waits the pump prime time, 2 s by default. It stops the pump after the valves close. WARNING: Set the kill switch to off before you work on the pump. While the kill switch is on, the controller can start the pump at any time. CAUTION: Fill the tank before the first shot. A pump that runs dry can lose its prime and get damage.
data_description.main_line_switch: The valve on the shared supply line to all the zones. Map it when the plumbing above has a main-line valve. Leave it EMPTY when it does not. The controller opens the main-line valve before the zone valve. It waits the main-line lead time, 1 s by default. It closes the main-line valve after the zone valve closes.
data_description.waste_switch: An optional waste or recirculation valve. The integration records it. The valve must read off before a setup change can save. By default the controller does not operate this valve. With the Waste valve rule of the room set to Check closed, no shot starts while it reads open; set to Close for each shot, the controller switches it off before each shot and never opens it. Otherwise, if the plumbing needs this valve closed to send the feed to the plants, close it yourself. Leave the field empty if the room has no waste valve. CAUTION: Close the waste valve before the shots start. An open waste valve can send the feed to waste, and the plants get less water.
data_description.light_entity: The light entity of the room. Day and night come from the lights-on and lights-off hours, not from this entity. The controller does not operate the light. The controller checks it against the lights hours and reports a disagreement that continues for 15 min or more. Select the entity that shows the state of the grow light. Make sure that the lights hours agree with the light timer.
data_description.lights_on_hour: The hour, from 0 to 23, when the lights come on. The grow-day starts at this hour. At lights-on, the controller resets the daily water and shot counters of each zone. The zones move from P3 to P0 at this hour. Enter the hour that the light timer uses. Change this hour each time that the light timer changes. CAUTION: Do not set a lights-on hour that is different from the light timer. The controller then gives shots while the lights are off.
data_description.lights_off_hour: The hour, from 0 to 23, when the lights go off. At lights-off, the controller moves every zone to P3, the overnight dryback. Enter the hour that the light timer uses. Make sure that the lights hours agree with the light timer.
data_description.substrate_volume: The substrate volume of one plant, in litres. For example, enter 6 for a 6 L rockwool block. A new room starts at a generic value. The controller multiplies this volume by the plant count. The shot size is a percentage of that zone volume. Increase: each shot gives more water. Decrease: each shot gives less water. CAUTION: Do not keep the generic value. A wrong volume gives shots that are too large or too small for the substrate.
data_description.dripper_flow_rate: The flow of one dripper, in litres per hour. For example, enter 4 for a 4 L/h dripper. A new room starts at a generic value. The controller uses the dripper flow to calculate the shot duration. Increase: the shots get shorter. Decrease: the shots get longer. Do a catch test on some drippers. CAUTION: Do not enter a flow that is higher than the real flow. The shots are then too short, and the zone gets too little water.
data_description.drippers_per_plant: The number of drippers on each plant. A new room starts at a generic value. The controller multiplies this number by the plant count and the dripper flow to get the flow of the zone. Increase: the shots get shorter. Decrease: the shots get longer. Count the drippers on some plants. Enter the number that most plants have. CAUTION: Do not enter more drippers than the plants have. The shots are then too short, and the zone gets too little water.
data_description.field_capacity: The VWC of the substrate when it is full and drains freely, in %. The ramp does not go above field capacity, also when the peak target is higher. Increase: the ramp can go to a higher VWC. Decrease: the ramp stops at a lower VWC. Water a block until water drains from it. Wait until the drain stops. Read the VWC of the block. Enter that value.
data_description.max_ec: The highest safe pore EC for the substrate, in mS/cm. When pore EC reaches this value, the controller gives a flush shot with feed to dilute the substrate. Increase: the controller flushes at a higher pore EC. Decrease: it flushes at a lower pore EC. Set this value above the pore EC that you steer to. After a change, compare the pore EC of each zone with this value. CAUTION: Do not set the maximum safe EC too high. Salt can build up in the substrate before the controller flushes it.
data_description.temperature_sensor: An optional sensor for the temperature of the room or the canopy. The dashboard shows it on the history chart of the zone page. The controller does not use this sensor. Select a sensor at canopy height. Leave the field empty if the room has no temperature sensor.
data_description.humidity_sensor: An optional sensor for the humidity of the room. The dashboard shows it on the history chart of the zone page. The controller does not use this sensor. Leave the field empty if the room has no humidity sensor.
data_description.vpd_sensor: An optional sensor for the vapour pressure deficit (VPD) of the room. The dashboard shows it on the history chart of the zone page. The controller does not use this sensor. Leave the field empty if the room has no VPD sensor.
data_description.water_level_sensor: An optional sensor for the level of the reservoir or the tank. The integration records it as a read-only mapping. This field does not stop shots at a low tank level. The reservoir minimum uses the tank level that you map in Rooms and setup. Select the sensor that reads the tank level. To stop shots at a low tank level, map the tank level in Rooms and setup.
data_description.notification_service: An optional notify service. The integration records it only. This field does not send alerts. The Notifications page sets which phone gets which alerts. With no phone on that page, the controller sends its alerts to its own `notify_service` option. Configure the phones in Crop Steering → Settings & help → Notifications. Send a test push from that page.
data_description.tank_temperature_sensor: An optional read-only sensor for the temperature of the tank water, in °C, °F or K. It is not the room temperature. The dashboard shows this value. The integration does not operate anything with it. Select a sensor in the tank water. Leave the field empty if the tank has no temperature sensor.
data_description.tank_ec_sensor: An optional read-only sensor for the tank EC, in mS/cm or dS/m. The dashboard shows this value. This mapping does not start or change the EC half of the source-water gate. To stop shots on a bad feed EC, map the feed EC probe instead.
data_description.tank_ph_sensor: An optional read-only sensor for the tank pH. The dashboard shows this value. This mapping does not start or change the pH half of the source-water gate. To stop shots on a bad feed pH, map the feed pH probe instead.
data_description.tank_last_fill_sensor: An optional timestamp sensor or date-and-time helper that records the last fill of the tank. A helper must have the date, the time and a numeric epoch timestamp. The dashboard shows the time of the last fill. Do not select a level sensor. The last change of a level sensor is not a fill.
data_description.tank_fill_entity: An optional read-only switch or binary sensor that shows when the tank fills. The dashboard shows the state. The dashboard does not operate this entity. Select the entity that is on while the tank fills.
data_description.feed_ec_sensor: An EC probe in the feed, not in the substrate. The value can be in mS/cm, dS/m or µS/cm. The integration converts it. Mapped: the source-water gate stops shots when feed EC is outside the feed EC limits of the room. It also stops shots when the probe gives no reading for 30 min (the default). Empty: the EC half of the gate is off. Calibrate the probe before you map it. CAUTION: Keep the probe calibrated and in the feed. A probe that reads wrong can stop all shots, and the plants can dry out.
data_description.feed_ph_sensor: A pH probe in the feed, not in the substrate. Mapped: the source-water gate stops shots when feed pH is outside the feed pH limits of the room. A new room has limits of 5.5 to 6.5. The gate also stops shots when the probe gives no reading for 30 min (the default). Empty: the pH half of the gate is off. Calibrate the probe before you map it. Put the probe in the tank or the line that feeds the plants. CAUTION: Keep the probe calibrated and in the feed. A probe that reads wrong can stop all shots, and the plants can dry out.

data_description.pump_switch: The switch that runs the water pump. Map it when the plumbing above has a pump. Leave it EMPTY when it does not. The controller starts the pump before it opens the main-line valve and the zone valve. It waits the pump prime time, 2 s by default. It stops the pump after the valves close. WARNING: Set the kill switch to off before you work on the pump. While the kill switch is on, the controller can start the pump at any time. CAUTION: Fill the tank before the first shot. A pump that runs dry can lose its prime and get damage.
data_description.main_line_switch: The valve on the shared supply line to all the zones. Map it when the plumbing above has a main-line valve. Leave it EMPTY when it does not. The controller opens the main-line valve before the zone valve. It waits the main-line lead time, 1 s by default. It closes the main-line valve after the zone valve closes.
data_description.waste_switch: An optional waste or recirculation valve. The integration records it. The valve must read off before a setup change can save. By default the controller does not operate this valve. With the Waste valve rule of the room set to Check closed, no shot starts while it reads open; set to Close for each shot, the controller switches it off before each shot and never opens it. Otherwise, if the plumbing needs this valve closed to send the feed to the plants, close it yourself. Leave the field empty if the room has no waste valve. CAUTION: Close the waste valve before the shots start. An open waste valve can send the feed to waste, and the plants get less water.
data_description.light_entity: The light entity of the room. Day and night come from the lights-on and lights-off hours, not from this entity. The controller does not operate the light. The controller checks it against the lights hours and reports a disagreement that continues for 15 min or more. Select the entity that shows the state of the grow light. Make sure that the lights hours agree with the light timer.
data_description.lights_on_hour: The hour, from 0 to 23, when the lights come on. The grow-day starts at this hour. At lights-on, the controller resets the daily water and shot counters of each zone. The zones move from P3 to P0 at this hour. Enter the hour that the light timer uses. Change this hour each time that the light timer changes. CAUTION: Do not set a lights-on hour that is different from the light timer. The controller then gives shots while the lights are off.
data_description.lights_off_hour: The hour, from 0 to 23, when the lights go off. At lights-off, the controller moves every zone to P3, the overnight dryback. Enter the hour that the light timer uses. Make sure that the lights hours agree with the light timer.
data_description.substrate_volume: The substrate volume of one plant, in litres. For example, enter 6 for a 6 L rockwool block. A new room starts at a generic value. The controller multiplies this volume by the plant count. The shot size is a percentage of that zone volume. Increase: each shot gives more water. Decrease: each shot gives less water. CAUTION: Do not keep the generic value. A wrong volume gives shots that are too large or too small for the substrate.
data_description.dripper_flow_rate: The flow of one dripper, in litres per hour. For example, enter 4 for a 4 L/h dripper. A new room starts at a generic value. The controller uses the dripper flow to calculate the shot duration. Increase: the shots get shorter. Decrease: the shots get longer. Do a catch test on some drippers. CAUTION: Do not enter a flow that is higher than the real flow. The shots are then too short, and the zone gets too little water.
data_description.drippers_per_plant: The number of drippers on each plant. A new room starts at a generic value. The controller multiplies this number by the plant count and the dripper flow to get the flow of the zone. Increase: the shots get shorter. Decrease: the shots get longer. Count the drippers on some plants. Enter the number that most plants have. CAUTION: Do not enter more drippers than the plants have. The shots are then too short, and the zone gets too little water.
data_description.field_capacity: The VWC of the substrate when it is full and drains freely, in %. The ramp does not go above field capacity, also when the peak target is higher. Increase: the ramp can go to a higher VWC. Decrease: the ramp stops at a lower VWC. Water a block until water drains from it. Wait until the drain stops. Read the VWC of the block. Enter that value.
data_description.max_ec: The highest safe pore EC for the substrate, in mS/cm. When pore EC reaches this value, the controller gives a flush shot with feed to dilute the substrate. Increase: the controller flushes at a higher pore EC. Decrease: it flushes at a lower pore EC. Set this value above the pore EC that you steer to. After a change, compare the pore EC of each zone with this value. CAUTION: Do not set the maximum safe EC too high. Salt can build up in the substrate before the controller flushes it.
data_description.temperature_sensor: An optional sensor for the temperature of the room or the canopy. The dashboard shows it on the history chart of the zone page. The controller does not use this sensor. Select a sensor at canopy height. Leave the field empty if the room has no temperature sensor.

data_description.feed_ec_sensor: An EC probe in the feed, not in the substrate. The value can be in mS/cm, dS/m or µS/cm. The integration converts it. Mapped: the source-water gate stops shots when feed EC is outside the feed EC limits of the room. It also stops shots when the probe gives no reading for 30 min (the default). Empty: the EC half of the gate is off. Calibrate the probe before you map it. CAUTION: Keep the probe calibrated and in the feed. A probe that reads wrong can stop all shots, and the plants can dry out.
data_description.feed_ph_sensor: A pH probe in the feed, not in the substrate. Mapped: the source-water gate stops shots when feed pH is outside the feed pH limits of the room. A new room has limits of 5.5 to 6.5. The gate also stops shots when the probe gives no reading for 30 min (the default). Empty: the pH half of the gate is off. Calibrate the probe before you map it. Put the probe in the tank or the line that feeds the plants. CAUTION: Keep the probe calibrated and in the feed. A probe that reads wrong can stop all shots, and the plants can dry out.

edit_parameters.title: Irrigation settings
edit_parameters.description: A short form for the most used settings. The same settings are on the dashboard as number entities. Change one setting at a time. Examine the zones for one grow-day after each change.

data_description.substrate_volume: The substrate volume of one plant, in litres. For example, enter 6 for a 6 L rockwool block. A new room starts at a generic value. The controller multiplies this volume by the plant count. The shot size is a percentage of that zone volume. Increase: each shot gives more water. Decrease: each shot gives less water. CAUTION: Do not keep the generic value. A wrong volume gives shots that are too large or too small for the substrate.
data_description.dripper_flow_rate: The flow of one dripper, in litres per hour. For example, enter 4 for a 4 L/h dripper. A new room starts at a generic value. The controller uses the dripper flow to calculate the shot duration. Increase: the shots get shorter. Decrease: the shots get longer. Do a catch test on some drippers. CAUTION: Do not enter a flow that is higher than the real flow. The shots are then too short, and the zone gets too little water.
data_description.p1_target_vwc: The VWC that ends the ramp (P1), in %. When a zone reaches the peak target, the zone moves to maintenance (P2). Increase: the ramp gives more water and the zone starts maintenance at a higher VWC. Decrease: the ramp ends at a lower VWC. Keep the peak target above the re-water point. CAUTION: Do not set the peak target near field capacity without a reason. A high peak target gives more runoff and wetter roots.
data_description.p2_vwc_threshold: The VWC that starts a maintenance shot in P2, in %. Increase: maintenance shots come more often and the zone stays wetter. Decrease: the zone dries back more between maintenance shots. Keep the re-water point some points below the peak target. A re-water point near the peak target gives many small shots. CAUTION: Do not set the re-water point too low. The zone can dry out before the next maintenance shot.

abort.setup_invalid:
The wizard stopped because it could not save the setup: {error}

Read the reason in the message. Correct the cause. Start the wizard again.
abort.reserved_room_name: The name "Default" is for the original room only. The wizard stopped. Start the wizard again. Enter a different room name.

error.setup_invalid:
Setup not saved: {error}

Read the reason in the message. Correct the field or the switch that the message names. Select Submit again.

kill_switch_missing.title: Crop Steering: Kill switch missing (CS-601)
kill_switch_missing.description:
The kill switch of this room is `{kill_switch}` ({source}). It does not exist in Home Assistant. The controller does not water any zone in this room.

If the room comes from an installation before the setup wizard, create the helper. Go to Settings → Devices & Services → Helpers → Create Helper → Toggle. Give the helper a name that makes the entity ID {kill_switch}. Do not create a helper for a room that the setup wizard made. That room stops on its own Engine Enabled switch.

CAUTION: Keep the new helper off until the zone map is correct. When the helper is on, the controller can start shots.

Code CS-601. What it means and what to do: Crop Steering → Help & tools → Error codes.

engine_switch_not_gate.title: Crop Steering: Separate kill switch (CS-610)
engine_switch_not_gate.description:
The controller stops this room on `{kill_switch}`. The Engine Enabled switch of the room, `{engine_switch}`, does not stop water. When you set Engine Enabled to off, the shots continue.

To stop water now, set `{kill_switch}` to off. To make Engine Enabled the kill switch, read "Moving a room's kill switch" in the install guide. For a room with no saved setup, set the `enable_flag` option of the controller app. For a room with a saved setup, change the kill switch in its setup.

WARNING: Do not use Engine Enabled to stop water before you work on the plumbing. Shots can start while Engine Enabled is off.

Code CS-610. What it means and what to do: Crop Steering → Help & tools → Error codes.

engine_offline.title: Crop Steering: No controller heartbeat (CS-602)
engine_offline.description:
The integration has no fresh heartbeat from the controller for more than 10 min. The entity `sensor.crop_steering_ai_heartbeat` is missing or old. The integration makes the entities, but only the controller steers. No automatic shots occur while the controller does not run.

Install or start the Crop Steering Controller app. Read the log of the app. With Home Assistant Container or Core, read the log of the controller container. If you use only manual control, you can ignore this alert.

CAUTION: Do not ignore this alert in a room with plants. With no controller, the zones get no shots and can dry out.

Code CS-602. What it means and what to do: Crop Steering → Help & tools → Error codes.

zone_no_sensor.title: Crop Steering: Zone without VWC probe (CS-603)
zone_no_sensor.description:
Zone(s) {zones} have no VWC probe mapped. The controller cannot steer these zones.

Go to Settings → Devices & Services → Crop Steering → Configure → Edit zones & hardware. Map a VWC probe for each of these zones.

Code CS-603. What it means and what to do: Crop Steering → Help & tools → Error codes.

fused_sensor_unavailable.title: Crop Steering: Zone probe unavailable (CS-604)
fused_sensor_unavailable.description:
The moisture (VWC) reading of zone(s) {zones} is unavailable. The probes can be offline or have the wrong entity ID. The moisture decisions for these zones have no zone reading.

Open Developer Tools → States. Find each probe of the zone and read its state. Make sure that the zone map has the correct probe entities.

Code CS-604. What it means and what to do: Crop Steering → Help & tools → Error codes.

strategy_hold.title: Crop Steering: Grow plan holds steering (CS-606)
strategy_hold.description:
The grow plan of the room holds the steering of the zones that it manages: {reason}. Until the hold clears, the controller gives these zones only rescue shots, watchdog shots and minimum-daily shots.

Open the plan on the dashboard under Irrigation plan → Schedule. Correct the cause. If the plan stays in error, disarm the plan. Then arm the plan again.

CAUTION: Do not leave the hold for a long time. The zones get only safety shots and can dry back more than the plan wants.

Code CS-606. What it means and what to do: Crop Steering → Help & tools → Error codes.

strategy_degraded.title: Crop Steering: Plan day not applied (CS-607)
strategy_degraded.description:
The grow plan could not apply the current day at lights-on: {reason}. The plan keeps its last valid targets, and the controller continues to steer. The plan tries again every minute. A plan that waits to start stays armed.

Correct the cause. The usual cause is an old controller heartbeat or an old probe reading. The card clears when the cause is gone.

Code CS-607. What it means and what to do: Crop Steering → Help & tools → Error codes.

entities_moved.title: Crop Steering: {count} setting(s) not found (CS-605)
entities_moved.description:
The controller finds each setting by its exact entity ID. The settings below have a different entity ID. The controller uses its built-in defaults for them.

{entities}

The built-in defaults apply, also for the daily water cap and the plant count. The shots can be wrong for the zones.

Keep the kill switch off until you correct the entity IDs. If you changed an entity ID, change it back. Go to Settings → Devices & services → Entities. Select the entity. Select the cog. Enter the old ID in Entity ID. If almost every entity is in the list, delete the Crop Steering entry. Restart Home Assistant. Add Crop Steering again. The integration does not rename an entity for you.

CAUTION: Keep the kill switch off until the card clears. The defaults can give too much or too little water to the zones.

Code CS-605. What it means and what to do: Crop Steering → Help & tools → Error codes.

max_run_latch.title: Crop Steering: Shots at maximum length (CS-312)

confirm.title: Water these zones again
confirm.description:
The last shots of zone(s) {zones} all needed more time than the maximum shot length of the room. The controller cut each shot to the maximum length. These zones get less water than their shot size asks for. {what}

Examine the probe of the zone. A probe that is stuck dry asks for long shots. Examine the substrate volume and the dripper flow of the zone. If they are correct, increase the maximum shot length of the room.

Code CS-312. What it means and what to do: Crop Steering → Help & tools → Error codes.

Zone(s) {zones} start to get shots again at the next check of the controller. Do this only after you find the cause. If the zones continue to hit the maximum length, the controller stops them again.

abort.room_not_loaded: This room is not loaded now. Reload the Crop Steering integration. Then try again.

stock_low.title: Crop Steering: {count} stock tank(s) low (CS-608)
stock_low.description:
These stock tanks are at or below their low mark:

{tanks}

Each batch tank that the room makes takes a dose from every stock tank.

Refill the stock tanks. Open Crop Steering → Stock tanks. Press Refilled, or enter the level that you read on the tank. The card clears when every tank is above its low mark.

Code CS-608. What it means and what to do: Crop Steering → Help & tools → Error codes.

outside_zone_bounds.title: Crop Steering: {count} setting(s) above zone limit (CS-611)
outside_zone_bounds.description:
The limits of the daily water and the maximum shot length now follow the size of each zone. The size comes from the plants, the litres per plant and the dripper flow. These settings were already above the new limit:

{settings}

The controller keeps these settings and uses them as before. Nothing changes until you edit one of them. A new value must then be in the limit.

Examine the plants, the litres per plant and the dripper flow of each zone in Rooms and setup. If a zone size is too small, correct it. The limit then follows. The card clears when each setting is in its limit.

Code CS-611. What it means and what to do: Crop Steering → Help & tools → Error codes.

dosing_get.name: Read dosing
dosing_get.description: Returns the dosing pumps, the batch hardware, the recipe and the feed schedule of the room. It also gives the request that waits for the controller and the entities that the setup can use. Changes nothing. It has no administrator check. Use it to read the revision before `dosing_save`.

room_id.name: Room ID
room_id.description: The canonical ID of the room: `room:` for the default room, or `room:` and the room prefix for a named room. A different ID reads a different room. The integration refuses an unknown ID. Example: `room:f1_` for a named room, or `room:` for the default room.

dosing_save.name: Save dosing setup
dosing_save.description: Replaces the dosing pumps, the batch hardware and the recipe of the room. Changes stored data only. It does not start a pump. The integration refuses the save while a request waits, while a dose or a batch is in progress, or when the revision is old. When a signed-in user calls it, that user must be a Home Assistant administrator. An automation can call it without this check. Read the revision with `dosing_get` first. After the save, examine the setup on the "Dosing" page. CAUTION: Make sure that each pump entity and each recipe quantity is correct. A wrong setup can dose the wrong stock solution into the batch tank.

room_id.name: Room ID
room_id.description: The canonical ID of the room: `room:` for the default room, or `room:` and the room prefix for a named room. A different ID saves the setup of a different room. The integration refuses an unknown ID. Example: `room:f1_` for a named room, or `room:` for the default room.

expected_revision.name: Expected revision
expected_revision.description: The revision that `dosing_get` returned before this change. When the stored revision is different, the integration refuses the call and changes nothing. Read the revision with `dosing_get` immediately before the call. Minimum: 0.

pumps.name: Dosing pumps
pumps.description: Up to 8 dosing pumps, in the order of the "Dosing" page. The stored pumps become this list. Each pump has a maximum dose in mL. A pump without an ID gets an ID from its name.

batch.name: Batch setup
batch.description: The fill, mix and hold hardware of the batch tank, and the recipe. The stored batch setup becomes this object. See `docs/DOSING.md` for the format.

feed.name: Feed schedule
feed.description: The named feed recipes, the recipe for each week of the grow, and the recipe that a person selected. Empty: the integration keeps the stored feed schedule. Optional. The week count starts on the day that the first week starts.

profile.name: Hardware profile
profile.description: The dosing times and limits of the room. They include the wait for a shot in progress, the readback times and the sensor timeout. They also include the lowest calibrated flow and the longest dose. A value that you leave out takes its default. Empty: the integration keeps the stored profile. Optional. The longest dose has a default of 1200 s and a range of 60 to 3600 s.

dosing_request.name: Request a dose or batch
dosing_request.description: Asks the controller to dose one pump into the batch tank, to make a batch, or to stop. A dose or a batch runs dosing pumps with stock solutions. A stop replaces any request that waits. The integration refuses a dose or a batch while a different request waits. The controller does not act on a request older than 120 s. A dose or a batch needs an administrator when a signed-in user calls it. Any signed-in user can ask for a stop. An automation can call it without this check. Use the "Dosing" page for this. Give the pump and the quantity for a dose. WARNING: Do not request a dose or a batch while a person works at the batch tank. The pumps can start, and the chemicals can cause injury. CAUTION: Make sure that the dose quantity is correct before you send it. Too much stock solution can damage the plants.

room_id.name: Room ID
room_id.description: The canonical ID of the room: `room:` for the default room, or `room:` and the room prefix for a named room. A different ID doses in a different room. The integration refuses an unknown ID. Example: `room:f1_` for a named room, or `room:` for the default room.

action.name: Action
action.description: What to do: `dose`, `batch` or `stop`. Dose: one pump runs. Batch: the controller makes a batch. Stop: the controller stops the dosing. Example: `stop`.

pump.name: Pump ID
pump.description: The ID of the pump to run, for a dose. A different ID runs a different pump. Necessary for a dose only. Get the ID from `dosing_get`.

ml.name: Dose quantity
ml.description: The quantity to dose, in mL. Increase: the pump gives more stock solution. Decrease: the pump gives less. Necessary for a dose only. Give more than 0 mL, up to the maximum of the pump. The field accepts up to 5000 mL. Example: 25.

run_anyway.name: Run anyway
run_anyway.description: For a batch only: a test refill that an administrator examined and asks for anyway. On: the integration stores the request with this flag. The controller still refuses the batch for each safety reason. Default: off. The integration refuses this flag on a dose or a stop.

notify_get.name: Read notifications
notify_get.description: Returns who gets which alerts: the row of each phone, the alert types, and the phones of the site with their owners. Changes nothing. It has no administrator check. The answer also shows if the caller can change every row. Use it to read the revision before `notify_save`.

notify_save.name: Save notifications
notify_save.description: Saves who gets which alerts. Each phone row gives the alert types, the rooms, high priority and the digest. Changes who gets a notification. It does not change shots. An administrator can change every row and the room settings. A different signed-in user can change only the alert types, rooms, high priority and digest of their own phones. An automation saves as an administrator. Read the revision with `notify_get` first. After the save, send a test with `notify_test`.

expected_revision.name: Expected revision
expected_revision.description: The revision that `notify_get` returned. When the stored revision is different, the integration refuses the save and changes nothing. Read the revision with `notify_get` immediately before the save. Minimum: 0.

recipients.name: Recipients
recipients.description: The row of each phone: service, name, user ID, alert types, rooms, high priority and digest. The stored rows become this list. Maximum: 20 rows. Example: one row for `notify.mobile_app_my_phone`.

idle_hours.name: Hours without water
idle_hours.description: The time after which a room with no shot gets an alert. The room must be on, with its lights on and a zone in P1 or P2. Increase: the alert comes later. Decrease: the alert comes sooner. Default: 3 h. Range: 1 to 12 h. Only an administrator can change it.

digest_hours.name: Hours between digests
digest_hours.description: The time between two digest notifications to a phone that takes a digest. Increase: fewer digests, each with more items. Decrease: more digests, each with fewer items. Default: 4 h. Range: 1 to 24 h. Only an administrator can change it.

mutes.name: Muted rooms
mutes.description: A map from each room prefix to the time that its mute ends. A muted room sends only emergency notifications. The map replaces all mutes. Empty: the integration keeps the stored mutes. Use an ISO time with its offset, at most 30 days ahead. Only an administrator can mute a room. Example: the key `f1_` with the value `2026-10-20T08:00:00+13:00`.

notify_test.name: Send a test notification
notify_test.description: Sends one test notification to a phone. An administrator can test any phone. A different signed-in user can test only their own phones. Use it after you add a phone. Make sure that the phone shows the notification.

service.name: Notify service
service.description: The notify service of the phone. A different service sends the test to a different phone. Example: `notify.mobile_app_my_phone`.

notify.name: Send a notification
notify.description: Sends one notification to each phone whose row includes the alert type and the room. The controller calls it for its alerts, its phase changes and the settings that the AI assistant changes. When a signed-in user calls it, that user must be a Home Assistant administrator. An automation or the controller can call it without this check. Use it in an automation to send your own alert to the same phones.

key.name: Key
key.description: What the notification is about. A later notification with the same key replaces this one on the phone. Example: `stock_low`.

code.name: CS code
code.description: The CS code of the alert. The code sets the alert types that the notification belongs to. A different code can send the notification to different phones. Optional. Example: CS-608.

event.name: Event
event.description: The event type, for a notification that is not an alert: `phase` (a zone changed phase) or `jev_setpoint` (the AI assistant moved a setting). The event sets which phones get the notification. Optional. Leave it empty for an alert.

room.name: Room prefix
room.description: The prefix of the room: empty for the default room, `f1_` for a named room. Only phones whose rows include this room, or all rooms, get the notification. Without a room, each phone with the alert type gets it. Optional. Example: `f1_`.

zone.name: Zone
zone.description: The zone that the notification is about. The zone has no effect on which phones get the notification. Optional. Range: 1 to 64. Example: 2.

title.name: Title
title.description: The title of the notification. The phone shows this title. Example: Stock tank low.

message.name: Message
message.description: The text of the notification. The phone shows this text. Example: The balance tank has 2 L left.

urgent.name: Urgent
urgent.description: On marks a critical alert. On: a phone whose row asks for high priority gets a high-priority notification, also for a muted room. Off: a normal notification. Default: off.

overlays.name: AI changes
overlays.description: The entity IDs of the settings that the AI assistant just changed. The notification gets Keep and Undo buttons on a phone with the Home Assistant app. Optional. Example: `["number.crop_steering_zone_1_p2_shot_size"]`.
